chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from a worker who was with Muhammad ibn Rashid, who said:

I attended the evening meal of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the summer. A tray was brought with bread, and a bowl was brought containing tharid (bread soaked in broth) and boiling meat. He placed his hand in it and found it hot, then raised it while saying: 'We seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah from the Fire. We cannot bear this, so how can we bear the Fire?' He kept repeating this until the bowl was cool enough to touch, so he placed his hand in it, and we placed our hands when it was possible for us, so he ate and we ate with him.

Then the tray was removed, and he said: 'O boy, bring us something.' He was brought dates on a platter. I extended my hand, and they were dates, so I said: 'May Allah keep you well, this is the season of grapes and fruit.' He said: 'These are dates.' Then he said: 'Remove this and bring us something.' He was brought dates, I extended my hand and said: 'These are dates.' He said: 'They are good.'

key_terms.الْقَصْعَةُ: The bowl or dish: Referring to the container holding the food.
key_terms.ثَرِيدٌ: Tharid: A dish of bread soaked in meat broth, a common and valued food in early Islamic times.
key_terms.طَيِّبٌ: Good/Pleasant: Describing the quality or taste of the dates.
key_terms.نَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ: We seek refuge with Allah from the Fire: A phrase used here to connect physical heat to the heat of Hell.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's reaction to the heat of the food during his meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imams' use of *tadabbur* (contemplation) in daily life, where Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) employed the physical sensation of heat to evoke spiritual awareness of *Jahannam*. His repeated invocation of *Nasta'jir billah min an-nar* transforms a mundane act of eating into a lesson on humility and the fragility of human endurance compared to divine punishment. The subsequent appreciation for out-of-season dates further emphasizes the virtue of *shukr* (gratitude) for simple sustenance, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on mindfulness in everyday actions.

en.hubeali: H 14622 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbaar, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, from a worker of Muhammad Bin Rashid who said:

I was present at the evening meal of Ja’far Bin Muhammadasws during the summer. A tray of bread was brought to himasws, and a bowl of porridge and boiling meat. So heasws extended his hand towards it and found it to be hot. Then heasws raised hisasws hand and said: ‘Weasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire, weasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire. We are not strong enough (to bear) this, so how can we (bear) the Fire (of Hell)?’ And heasws went on repeating these words until it was possible to (touch) the bowl. So heasws placed hisasws in it (the hot food in front of himasws), and we placed our hands in it (our portion) when it was possible. So heasws ate, and we ate with himasws.

Then the (food) from the food-mat was taken away. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O young boy, bring us something’. So he came with the dates on a platter. I extended my hand, and there were dates, so I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well, this is the time (season) for the grapes and the apples’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘these are the dates’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take this away and bring us something’. So he came up with dates (another variety of dates). I extended my hand and said, ‘These are dates’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is good’.
